readiness_summary.summary: SHS/SHF V1 is strong enough for controlled private beta and operator rehearsal, but not ready for paid client launch or public SHF launch because several flows remain local/sample/draft, production auth is not present, and SHF public claims still require verified/public-approved data replacement.

tracks.name: SHS Public Website / Product Positioning
evidence: shrv1 exposes public launcher routes in src/entries/index.main.jsx.
shf-next exposes public /solutions and public studio template routes.
Some product positioning exists, but public SHS launch narrative is split across repos and pages.
blockers: Needs final public positioning pass and route-by-route copy approval.

tracks.name: SHS Sales Layer
evidence: shf-next includes SalesCommandCenter and ops command data that links sales handoffs into production work.
stable localStorage lifecycle keys are used for handoff continuity.
blockers: Local persistence and operator workflow are private-beta grade, not production sales operations.

tracks.name: SHS Production Ops
evidence: shf-next includes ProductionProjects and ops readiness data.
shrv1 includes admin Production Ops route families and sidebar links.
blockers: Needs production persistence, explicit operator runbook, and final route smoke before paid launch.

tracks.name: Development Team Library
evidence: shf-next DevelopmentLibrary supports active handoff context, blueprint selection, QA checklist, and build packet generation.
The flow keeps internal SHS methods out of client-facing copy.
blockers: Output is still local/operator-driven and needs release handoff discipline.

tracks.name: QA + Delivery
evidence: shf-next routes /ops/qa to QADeliveryDashboard.
ops readiness data detects QA blockers and delivery-ready states.
blockers: Needs final acceptance checklist, screenshot QA evidence retention, and launch signoff process.

tracks.name: SHS ClientOps Center
evidence: shf-next includes ClientOpsCenter under /ops/clientops.
ClientOps workflow tracks records, health, support tickets, monthly reviews, and upgrade opportunities.
blockers: Local persistence and internal-only access posture make it private-beta ready, not paid-client production ready.

tracks.name: Website Studio / WebMaker / Template Marketplace
evidence: shf-next keeps /studio/templates and /studio/templates/browse public.
shrv1 includes BuilderHub and WebMaker admin/public surfaces.
Template browsing and preview routes exist.
blockers: Template browsing is usable, but management/build/export workflow still needs clean V1 boundary and operator QA.

tracks.name: SHS Reporting Layer
evidence: shrv1 reporting admin surfaces include Truth/Oracle/readiness metadata.
Agent Fabric reports routes expose governed snapshots and readiness context.
blockers: Need final paid-client report workflow, report delivery policy, and sample-vs-verified labeling checks.

tracks.name: SHF Public Website / Foundation Positioning
evidence: shf-next exposes /foundation and /foundation/impact-report as public foundation surfaces.
The SHF report generator includes foundation positioning and public report preview.
blockers: Public narrative and proof claims need final approval before external launch.

tracks.name: SHF Command Center
evidence: shrv1 includes src/pages/shf-command/SHFImpactCommandCenter.jsx.
Command Center includes AI analyst/truth context drawer and impact map integration.
blockers: Command Center is internal/admin ready but needs live source replacement and browser smoke before external stakeholder demos.

tracks.name: SHF Impact Map
evidence: shrv1 SHFImpactOhioMap filters to public-approved counties.
src/data/shfImpactData.js labels current counties as Sample/Draft and not verified.
blockers: Map must stay sample/draft until approved verified SHF records replace current sample data.

tracks.name: SHF Data Approval Gateway
evidence: shf-next routes /foundation/data-approval with CrossAppAccessNotice.
Data approval and public-approval governance layers exist in shrv1.
blockers: Gateway is review-oriented and internal; production approval workflow and source-backed records are still required.

tracks.name: SHF Impact Reports / Premium Reports
evidence: shf-next includes ShfImpactReportGenerator with generic and premium report modes.
Premium print route exists at /foundation/impact-report/print?style=premium&period=annual.
Report UI displays data status, last verified, trust level, and public-approved record counts.
blockers: Report content currently relies on local sample data and must not be publicly released as verified.

tracks.name: Governance/Admin Control Surfaces
evidence: shrv1 has Master Layer Registry, Truth Spine freeze, Oracle, AI Guardrails, Game Theory, and governance check scripts.
Admin routes expose Truth Spine, Oracle, AI Guardrails, Game Theory, Agent Fabric, Registry, Reports, Command, Dashboard, and LOO surfaces.
blockers: No audit blocker for private beta; continue to run governance checks before new architecture.

tracks.name: Identity / Access / Cross-App Bridge
evidence: shf-next uses CrossAppAccessNotice on internal /ops and /foundation/data-approval routes.
shf-next crossAppRouteBridge classifies template browsing and /solutions as public.
shrv1 includes identity/admin access routing files.
blockers: This is route classification and operator notice, not production authentication or authorization.

tracks.name: Agent Fabric / AI Governance UI
evidence: shrv1 includes Agent Fabric routers/services/tests for Truth Spine, Oracle, AI Guardrails, Game Theory, Reports, Watchtower, LOO, and newer governance layers.
Admin UI exposes Agent Fabric and governance pages.
blockers: Production API deployment, monitoring, and auth are outside current V1 audit scope.

tracks.name: End-to-End SHS Client Journey
evidence: Sales to handoff to production to development library to QA to ClientOps is represented in shf-next ops flow.
shrv1 admin surfaces support production operations and governance visibility.
blockers: Needs a rehearsed private-beta client scenario, production persistence, and acceptance gates.

tracks.name: End-to-End SHF Impact Journey
evidence: SHF data spine, map, command center, data approval, and reports exist across shrv1 and shf-next.
Public-facing filters and sample/draft labels reduce leakage risk.
blockers: Needs verified source intake, approval gateway pass, public approval, and report-ready data before public launch.

tracks.name: Build / QA / Deployment Readiness
evidence: shrv1 package scripts include build and extensive governance checks.
shf-next package includes build and lint scripts.
blockers: Need deploy target checklist, environment handling, and final route/browser smoke package.

tracks.name: Documentation / Operator Readiness
evidence: shrv1 contains extensive governance docs, staging reports, audit reports, and layer V1 docs.
Current docs emphasize anti-drift controls and route/staging discipline.
blockers: Need short operator runbooks for private beta, paid launch, public SHF release, and rollback.

private_beta: Run a complete SHS client journey rehearsal with one realistic account.
Run a complete SHF impact journey rehearsal with sample records clearly labeled.
Prepare operator runbooks for each internal route cluster.
Record browser smoke evidence for critical routes.
paid_client_launch: Add production auth/role enforcement or confirmed launch-safe access boundaries.
Replace local-only lifecycle persistence with approved production persistence or documented beta constraints.
Define client acceptance and report delivery signoff gates.
Confirm no internal SHS method language leaks into client-facing outputs.
public_shf_launch: Replace sample/draft SHF impact records with verified, public-approved, report-ready records.
Run Data Approval Gateway and public approval review.
Confirm public map/report routes only expose approved SHF data.
Complete foundation narrative and claim approval.
post_v1: Move from local scaffolds to durable services where needed.

seven_day_private_beta: Day 1: freeze route inventory and assign owners for SHS and SHF critical paths.
Day 2: run SHS sales-to-ClientOps rehearsal using one realistic account.
Day 3: run SHF source-to-report rehearsal using sample records with labels intact.
Day 4: browser smoke all public and internal routes; capture blockers.
Day 5: write operator runbooks for Sales, Production, QA, ClientOps, Data Approval, and Reports.
Day 6: fix only launch blockers that do not create new architecture.
Day 7: run governance/build validations and owner go/no-go review.
fourteen_day_v1_launch: Add route smoke checklist and owner signoff checklist.
Finalize client-facing copy and public/private leakage scan.
Confirm paid-client launch constraints and beta disclaimers.
Verify report and approval labels on all SHF public surfaces.
Run full builds in shrv1 and shf-next before launch decision.
thirty_day_polish: Move approved local workflows toward durable persistence.
Strengthen production auth and role enforcement.
Automate browser route checks and bad-text scans.
Replace SHF sample data with verified approved records as available.

top_5_highest_roi_next_tasks: Run and document one end-to-end SHS client journey rehearsal from sales intake to ClientOps.
Run and document one end-to-end SHF impact journey from data approval to premium report.
Create a route smoke checklist for shrv1 admin/public and shf-next public/internal routes.
Write private-beta operator runbooks for Sales, Production Ops, QA, ClientOps, Reports, and SHF Data Approval.
Replace or clearly quarantine all SHF sample/draft public impact records before any public SHF launch.

findings: shf-next public template routes are classified public and do not use CrossAppAccessNotice.
shf-next internal ops and foundation data approval routes use CrossAppAccessNotice.
SHF impact data filters public-approved records and labels current records Sample/Draft.
Paid-client and public-SHF launch still require final route/browser copy scan.
risks: Public SHF report output is presentation-ready visually, but current data remains sample/draft.
Internal SHS operations are protected by route boundary notices, not production-grade auth.
